Sarasavi Uyana College produced an impressive performance to defeat Hemamali Girls’ School 32/10 in the inaugural “Singha Denuwange Ran Satana” 12-a-side girls’ rugby big match, played at 

the Bogambara Grounds in Kandy recently.

Hemamali made the early breakthrough through Chaturika Ranaweera, while Tisali Perera replied for Sarasavi Uyana. At the short breather it was 10 apiece.

Sarasavi Uyana raised the tempo after the break, adopting an attacking approach and putting the Hemamali defence under pressure. Isanka, Kaumodi, Umasha and Bimasa crossed the line, with a successful conversion helping the winners complete a 32-point tally. Heshan Gamage coached the winning outfit. Deepal Punyawardena refereed. Isanka Weeraperakrama won the Player of the Match award while Gayathri Sanganayaka won the Rising 

Star award. (SJ)

title: Under19 WC record holder Viran Chamuditha to lead Sri Lanka | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 31 October 2026 00:00
-     - 7

Sri Lanka’s Under19 World Cup record holder for the highest individual score Viran Chamuditha will lead a 15-member squad to the Under19 Men’s 50-over Asia Cup to be held in Oman from 5-14 November.

Senuka Wekunagoda, a top order left-hand batsman from St Joseph’s College, Colombo will be his vice-captain.

Chamuditha created history by smashing 192 off 142 balls against Japan which stands as the highest individual score in Under19 Men’s World Cup history. A product of St Servatius College, Matara, Chamuditha is a left-hand batsman and a slow left-arm orthodox bowler.  

Sri Lanka are in Group B alongside Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Malaysia. Group A comprises India, Nepal, Pakistan and UAE.

Sri Lanka opens their Under19 Men’s Asia Cup campaign when they meet Malaysia in the opening match of the tournament on 5 November. Sri Lanka’s other group matches are on 7 November against Bangladesh and on 9 November against Afghanistan. The top two teams in the group qualify for the semi-finals. The team will leave for Oman on 2 November.

The squad: Viran Chamuditha (Captain), Senuja Wekunagoda (Vice-Captain), Rehan Peiris, Kithma Widanapathirana, Gimhan Rasanjana, Sanul Weeraratne, Chaniru Senaratne, Lithma Perera, Vigneshwaran Akash, Sethmika Seneviratne, Gimhan Mendis, Lathendra Akash, Himaru Deshan, Stevon Peiris, Kaushika Kumarasinghe

title: Sri Lanka commence Hong Kong Sixes with thrilling win | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 31 October 2026 00:00
-     - 11

Bangladesh went through a most disheartening opening day of the Hong Kong International Sixes at Mong Kok yesterday when they lost both their Group B matches by one wicket to Scotland and Sri Lanka respectively.

Bangladesh made 94 against Scotland, but the Scots buoyed by a brilliant 53* off 20 balls (3 fours, 6 sixes) by their captain Finlay McCreath romped home to win by one wicket off the last ball. In their second match of the day, Bangladesh put up a better batting performance scoring 127-4 with Habibur Rahman scoring 57 off 15 balls (3 fours, 7 sixes), but still ended on the losing side as Sri Lanka topped that score to win by one wicket with four balls to spare.

Vishen Halambage was Sri Lanka’s match winner with a blistering 80* off 17 balls that comprised 11 sixes and 3 fours. Sri Lanka and Scotland meet today at 7.10 am to vie for the top spot in Group B.

In the other upsets of the day UAE beat Pakistan by one wicket, but Pakistan recovered in their second game to defeat arch rivals India by 4 wickets. South Africa suffered two back to back defeats at the hands of Oman and Afghanistan to finish bottom of Group D. England also went out of the Cup final when they were beaten by Hong Kong and Australia to finish at the bottom of Group A. The tournament continues on its second day today.

title: Everton beat Newcastle to set up League Cup  quarterfinal with Fleetwood | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 31 October 2026 00:00
-     - 12

The Merseyside club eased through despite the absence of midfielder Jack Grealish, who was dropped from the squad following an internal breach of club discipline

Everton advanced to the League Cup quarterfinals with a 3-1 victory over Newcastle United, setting up a clash against fourth-tier side Fleetwood Town.

First-half goals from James Garner and Hayden Hackney put the hosts in control before Thierno Barry struck after the break at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, with Dan Burn scoring late for the visitors on Thursday.

The Merseyside club eased through despite the absence of midfielder Jack Grealish, who was dropped from the squad following an internal breach of club discipline. Prime Minister Andy Burnham, an Everton supporter, was among the crowd. Everton will travel to League Two side Fleetwood, who stunned Premier League champions Arsenal on Tuesday. Mikel Arteta’s side crashed out 5-3 on penalties in an incredible fourth-round upset after the tie finished 1-1 in normal time.

Crystal Palace will welcome Sunderland, while Bournemouth will play away at Liverpool, who beat Chelsea 6-5 in a dramatic penalty shootout on Wednesday. Defending champions Manchester City will take on third-tier side Bradford City. They avoided the fate that befell Arsenal and stayed on course to retain their title by twice coming from behind to draw 2-2 against Brighton, then triumph 4-3 in the shootout.

The quarterfinals are scheduled to take place in the week beginning 14 December.

title: Ronaldo closes in on 1,000th goal with hat-trick | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 31 October 2026 00:00
-     - 9

Cristiano Ronaldo

Cristiano Ronaldo’s hat-trick helped Al-Nassr to a 5-3 win against Al-Kholood in the Saudi Pro League and took the Portugal striker to 985 career goals. With the game evenly poised at 2-2 following goals from Angelo Gabriel and Sadio Mane for Al-Nassr, Ronaldo secured the win for his side by scoring three times in 15 second-half minutes.

His Portugal team-mate Joao Felix contributed four assists, including for two of Ronaldo’s goals. It was the 67th hat-trick of the 41-year-old’s career as he continues to chase another milestone in a glittering career. He has scored seven of his hat-tricks for Al-Nassr - along with 44 for Real Madrid, 10 for Portugal and three each at Manchester United and Juventus.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner has won league titles in England, Spain, Italy and Saudi Arabia and is the all-time top goal-scorer in men’s international football. He has spent almost four years at Saudi Pro League champions Al-Nassr, with whom he has one year remaining on his contract.

In August, he hinted at retirement by saying it was “probably” his last year playing. Al-Nassr are defending champions in the Saudi Pro League and sit second in the table, although they have a game in hand on leaders Al-Qadsiah.

title: Shock Basel loss dents Djokovic’s ATP Finals hopes | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 31 October 2026 00:00
-     - 9

Novak Djokovic

Novak Djokovic’s hopes of making a record 19th appearance at the ATP Finals have been dented by a surprise defeat against Jan-Lennard Struff at the Swiss Indoors in Basel.

Playing in the tournament for the first time in 15 years, the 39-year-old lost 6-7 (4-7) 7-5 7-6 (7-5) - the first time he has been beaten by Struff in nine meetings.

“I knew I needed to go for it. There was only one way to play it. So, I was very, very happy,” said the world number 27.

“I knew I had to play my best tennis to have a chance. The last eight times he beat me very, very easily. So, I’m very, very happy and pleased with the performance.”

The year’s top-eight performers qualify for the ATP event in Turin and this result leaves Djokovic - the men’s game’s record 24-time Grand Slam winner - 11th in the standings.

Djokovic admitted he expected to feel “a little rusty” after his win against Frenchman Ugo Humbert on Wednesday, but now faces a fight to make the finals as he is outside the top 10 for the first time since 2018. Rafael Jodar holds the final qualifying spot in ninth place, because number one Jannik Sinner is injured and will not take part.

Djokovic is 319 points behind Jodar, although he has the opportunity at the Paris Masters in November to move up the rankings. The Serb is aiming to move ahead of Roger Federer with his 19th appearance at the finals in Turin.

He has won the event a record seven times and has missed the past two editions with injury - but the last time he failed to qualify on merit was in 2017, when his season was affected by injury. Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton have their places confirmed for the showpiece event in Italy from 15-22 November, although American Shelton also surprisingly lost in Basel. The top seed lost 6-3 6-7 (4-7) 7-6 (7-1) to Swiss wildcard Jerome Kym, who is ranked 222nd in the world.

title: Stage set for a blockbuster final today | Daily FT
summary:
Saturday, 31 October 2026 00:00
-     - 9

Pakistan Captain Shaheen Afridi (left) and Sri Lanka Captain Kusal Mendis with the Tri-Series trophy

LAHORE: The stage is set for a blockbuster final of the ODI Tri-Series between Asian giants Pakistan and Sri Lanka at the Gaddafi Stadium here today after a week in which the hosts swung from one of their most dramatic wins in years to one of their most chastening defeats.

How Shaheen Afridi’s side responds to being bowled out for 110 will shape the outcome of a tournament that doubles as preparation for the 2027 World Cup. Pakistan’s route to the final went through Sunday’s one-wicket victory over England, in which Shadab Khan made an unbeaten 113 from number eight and shared an unbroken 89-run last-wicket stand with Haris Rauf to chase 242 from 154 for 9. That result secured qualification. Two days later, against Sri Lanka in the same city, the side looked like a different team as they were bowled out for 110 in 25.5 overs with left-arm seamer Dilshan Madushanka taking a career-best 5/34.

The contrast between the two matches raises the question of which version of Pakistan turns up on Saturday. The side that beat Sri Lanka by 37 runs in the opening match, thanks to Salman Ali Agha’s 107 and a disciplined pace attack, is capable of beating them again. But the top order has been a recurring concern across the tournament, and the middle order has been rescued by individual innings from Agha and Shadab rather than by a steady platform. Against a Sri Lanka side with a confident bowling group and a fresh sense of momentum, a collapse in the first 10 overs could prove decisive.

That win is dominant enough for Sri Lanka to go into the final with a slight psychological edge. That game aside, Sri Lanka’s dynamic big-hitting with the bat has lit the tournament up for them, especially that monstrous run chase of 430 against England. They have breached 330 twice this tournament, and boast of the top-scorer in Pavan Rathnayake.

This series has been the making of a new Sri Lankan star. A fortnight ago, Rathnayake was an unknown quantity, boasting of a handful of internationals and a heap of potential as yet unrealised. For the final, he is Sri Lanka’s talisman after lighting up the tournament. He has scored two big hundreds against England, demonstrating his dazzling ability as well as the nerve to hold his own under pressure. He has scored 350 runs, averaged 116.67, and struck at 123.67. It has been a perfect tri-series for the 24-year old, and on Saturday, it could get the perfect finish.

Sri Lanka’s bowling might not have had quite the same impact, but as Madushanka showed against Pakistan, it is capable of landing some devastating blows on its day. As far as handling the pressure of a final at the Gaddafi Stadium goes, Sri Lanka will be fairly confident they are up to the challenge.

Sri Lanka’s talisman Pavan Rathnayake, can he provide his team with a perfect finish
